title: KV: soft-quarantine page lifecycle with backpressure-aware release and eviction hysteresis
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: In high-fragmentation workloads we observed oscillation between aggressive eviction and immediate rehydration of recently-evicted pages, causing elevated I/O and CPU under moderate memory pressure. This PR introduces a lightweight page lifecycle (active -> stashed -> soft-quarantined -> released) to reduce churn, plus a backpressure-aware release path that defers low-value releases during transient pressure spikes.

Summary: Implement a 'soft-quarantine' state for KV pages that have been candidate-evicted but are kept in a compact, compressed slab for a configurable grace period. While in soft-quarantine pages consume less resident memory accounting but can be restored without full spill-reload. The eviction path now signals the scheduler about transient pressure via a ReleaseFence token; release decisions use hysteresis windows and tenant-fairness weights so we avoid repeated evict/rehydrate cycles for hot tails.

Key changes: - page lifecycle state machine and in-memory compact store (server/kv/cache/soft_quarantine.go) - eviction hysteresis in the evictor; introduces short-term holdback and time-decay scoring (server/kv/evictor/evictor.go) - backpressure-aware release router that uses metrics from the scheduler and autoscaler to throttle bulk releases (pkg/schedulers/backpressure_router.go) - metrics and traces for quarantine lifecycle and backpressure signals (server/kv/metrics/metrics.go) - unit + integration tests and a microbenchmark exercising oscillatory workloads (tests/kv/quarantine_test.go, benchmarks/kv/page_lifecycle_bench.go) - docs explaining configuration knobs and rollout guidance (docs/kv/quarantine.md)

Behavioral guarantees: - default config preserves existing memory accounting; quarantine is opt-in by cluster config. - under steady pressure the soft-quarantine reduces load by keeping recently-evicted pages cheap to restore (lower I/O). - under sustained pressure quarantined pages are progressively compacted and finally released once grace periods and tenant priorities allow.

Testing and results: Microbenchmarks on p3.xlarge-like nodes show a 22% reduction in average eviction-induced disk reads for our mixed chat+search workload and latency P95 improvements of ~8ms during eviction storms. CI includes unit tests, an integration test that simulates tenant skew, and a perf canary run.

Rollout plan: Feature gated behind 'kv_soft_quarantine' flag. Start on staging for 48 hours with default short grace, enable for canary tenants, then gradually increase grace period if metrics are favorable.

Related: ENG-1842 (eviction feedback loop), ENG-1907 (tenant fairness scheduling).

review_comments: Samir Patel: Can you clarify memory accounting while a page is in soft-quarantine? The change in flags should not affect existing reserved memory calculations.

Author (Maya Chen): Soft-quarantined pages are tracked via a separate compact-resident counter and do not count toward the 'active_resident_bytes' metric by default. We added an opt-in toggle to include them in accounting for legacy customers.
Lena Ortiz: The hysteresis windows look sensible but we should make tenant weights pluggable for dedicated clusters.
Author (Maya Chen): Added TenantWeight hook and documented configuration; default weights preserve previous behavior.
Diego Alvarez: CI flaked on the canary perf run; re-ran and the perf canary now passes. Approving change.
Samir Patel: Verified metrics and traces on staging; overall looks good. Approved and squash-merge recommended.
release_notes: Introduce optional 'soft-quarantine' page lifecycle for KV cache to reduce evict/rehydrate churn under transient memory pressure; adds eviction hysteresis and backpressure-aware release router. Feature is gated and off by default.
upgrade_instructions: Enable 'kv_soft_quarantine' in cluster config. Start with short grace period (5s) and monitor 'kv.quarantine.restore_rate' and 'kv.eviction.hysteresis_misses' metrics. See docs/kv/quarantine.md for step-by-step rollout.
follow_up_tasks: ENG-1980: evaluate compressed slab algorithms for longer-term quarantine retention

notes: This PR focuses on reducing churn for workloads with frequent temporal locality flips. It is intentionally conservative: quarantine durations and memory accounting are configurable so we can tune per-cluster behavior during rollout.
